why: I compared the builder brief with the verifier brief's probes and found two overlaps. First, builder step 2 gives input/output examples, "clamp(-5, 0, 100) is 0, clamp(140, 0, 100) is 100, clamp(50, 0, 100) is 50", and the lo === hi case. All of these also appear in the case list of the verifier's Check 1 script. Second, builder step 5 tells the builder to run `node -e "console.log(Object.keys(require('./math.js')))"` and confirm each name appears as a heading in README.md's API section. That is the same probe as verifier Check 3, which lists the exports from Object.keys and matches each against a README heading. Neither of these is a repo test, a command named by an expect line, or a test the builder writes itself, so the exemptions don't cover them. Running `npm test` is allowed, but these shared checks break the criterion.
